名称.日文: 関東鉄道キハ5010形気動車

日文.词条标题: 関東鉄道キハ5010形気動車
日文.首段: 関東鉄道キハ5010形気動車（かんとうてつどうキハ5010がたきどうしゃ）は、関東鉄道の通勤形気動車である。

章节.概要: 元国鉄キハ30形気動車をワンマン改造したキハ100形の置換え用として製造され、2017年2月25日に営業運転を開始している。製造元は新潟トランシスである。
章节.導入まで:
それまでの関東鉄道では、キハ2100形からキハ5000形までに至る完全新造の軽快気動車、あるいはキハ0形など既存車両のDMH17系からのエンジン換装においては、新潟原動機（現・IHI原動機）製のDMF13系のみを採用していたが、キハ2100形の一次車に関しては1993年の導入から20年以上経過、搭載されているエンジンの陳腐化が進んでいた。また、車内天井の照明もLEDを採用することになったが、LED照明は2010年代初頭では電車での採用が相次いでいた一方で気動車、とりわけ通勤向けの一般形気動車での採用が2016年時点においてもJR東海のキハ25形以外にほぼ無かったことから、まずは実際の車両に試験的に搭載して走行試験を実施することとなった。
新潟原動機製のDMF13系（DMF13HZ）に代わる新型エンジンを採用するに当たり、キハ2100形2101・2102の編成にて2101で後に本形式に搭載されるコマツ製のDMF11HZ系の一形式であるSA6D125-HE2形に換装、同時に車内天井の照明を蛍光灯からLEDに変更し、2016年4月から営業運転を行いながら長期の走行試験が実施された。
キハ2100形による走行試験を反映し、関東鉄道の車両としてコマツ製のDMF11HZ系エンジンとLED照明を実用化した事実上の量産形式として設計された。
章节.特徴:
キハ5000形をベースとする両運転台車だが、従来と比べて以下の点が異なる。

車両塗装を「関鉄ホワイト」と呼ばれる白色と常総線沿線の鬼怒川と小貝川をイメージした青色のツートンカラーに「豊かな大地に波打つ稲穂」をイメージした黄金色のラインを車体腰部に配置するともに、新緑の筑波山をイメージしたマークを運転室側にある片引戸の戸袋部分に配置
エンジンをコモンレール式燃料制御システムを搭載した小松製作所製の出力355馬力のSA6D125-HE2形に変更（小松製作所製のSA6D125系エンジンは私鉄として初めて採用）
LED式停車駅案内表示器が扉の片方のみに設置。設置されていない扉の上部には停車駅一覧のみ設置されている。
整理券発行機の設置位置を運賃箱付近の1箇所のみに変更
車内の天井照明のLED化
腰掛モケットの色がキハ2400形までの赤色に戻された
客用扉の窓支持方式もキハ2400形までの従来車両と同様に戻された
つり手を2段式の形状に変更
車内側の客用扉の上部に扉開閉予告灯を設置するとともに客用扉の戸尻側に黄色の注意喚起フィルムを貼付け
ワンマン機器の運賃表示器を液晶式に変更
台車は同じく動台車がNF01HD形、従台車がNF01HT形であるが、耐雪ブレーキを追加している
ワンマン運転対応については共通となる
章节.現在: 現在、キハ5011とキハ5012の計2両が在籍しており、常総線で運用されている。2017年2月26日から3月3日までの間は、関東鉄道ホームページにおいて本形式の運行予定時刻を掲載していた。

車内の天井照明のLED化
腰掛モケットの色がキハ2400形までの赤色に戻された
客用扉の窓支持方式もキハ2400形までの従来車両と同様に戻された

英文.词条标题: Kantō Railway KiHa 5010 series diesel railcar
英文.首段: The Kantō Railway KiHa 5010 series diesel railcar (かんとうてつどうキハ5010がたきどうしゃ) is a commuter-type diesel railcar of Kantō Railway.

章节.Overview: It was built to replace the KiHa 100 series, which were former JNR KiHa 30 type diesel railcars converted for one-man operation, and it began commercial operation on February 25, 2017. It was built by Niigata Transys.
章节.Until introduction:
Until then, Kantō Railway had adopted only the DMF13 series made by Niigata Power Systems (now IHI Power Systems) for its completely newly built lightweight diesel railcars from the KiHa 2100 series to the KiHa 5000 series, and for engine replacements from the DMH17 series in existing cars such as the KiHa 0 type; however, for the first batch of the KiHa 2100 series, more than 20 years had passed since their introduction in 1993, and the engines they carried had become increasingly obsolete. Also, it was decided to adopt LED for the interior ceiling lighting, but whereas LED lighting was being adopted in rapid succession in electric cars in the early 2010s, its adoption in diesel railcars—especially general-purpose commuter diesel railcars—was almost nonexistent as of 2016 except for JR Central's KiHa 25 type; therefore, it was decided to first install it experimentally in an actual car and carry out running tests.
When adopting a new engine to replace the Niigata Power Systems DMF13 series (DMF13HZ), in the KiHa 2100 series set of 2101 and 2102, 2101 was re-engined with the SA6D125-HE2 type, a form of the Komatsu DMF11HZ series that would later be installed in this type, and at the same time the interior ceiling lighting was changed from fluorescent to LED, and from April 2016 long-term running tests were carried out while in commercial operation.
Reflecting the running tests with the KiHa 2100 series, it was designed as the de facto mass-production type that put into practical use, for a Kantō Railway car, the Komatsu DMF11HZ series engine and LED lighting.
章节.Features:
It is a double-ended cab car based on the KiHa 5000 series, but it differs from the conventional cars in the following points.
The livery is a two-tone of a white called "Kantetsu White" and a blue evoking the Kinu River and Kokai River along the Jōsō Line, with a golden line evoking "rice ears waving over the rich earth" placed on the waist of the body, and a mark evoking the fresh green of Mount Tsukuba placed on the door pocket of the single sliding door on the driver's cab side.
The engine was changed to the Komatsu SA6D125-HE2 type, rated at 355 hp and equipped with a common-rail fuel control system (the first adoption of a Komatsu SA6D125 series engine by a private railway).
The LED-type next-station indicator is installed on only one of the doors. Above the door where it is not installed, only a list of stopping stations is installed.
The installation position of the numbered-ticket issuing machine was changed to only one place near the fare box.
LED conversion of the interior ceiling lighting.
The color of the seat upholstery was returned to the red used up to the KiHa 2400 series.
The window support method of the passenger doors was also returned to the same as the conventional cars up to the KiHa 2400 series.
The straps were changed to a two-tier shape.
A door-opening warning light was installed above the passenger doors on the interior side, and a yellow caution film was affixed to the door-pocket side of the passenger doors.
The fare display of the one-man equipment was changed to a liquid-crystal type.
For the bogies, as before, the powered bogie is the NF01HD type and the trailer bogie is the NF01HT type, but snow-resistant brakes have been added.
The one-man operation provisions are the same.
章节.Present: Currently, a total of two cars, KiHa 5011 and KiHa 5012, are in service, operating on the Jōsō Line. From February 26 to March 3, 2017, the scheduled operating times of this type were posted on the Kantō Railway website.
章节.References:
"Railway Fan" (Kōyūsha)
May 2017 issue, "The New-Type Car Introduced to Replace the KiHa 100 Series: Kantō Railway KiHa 5010 Series."

英文.全文:
The Kantō Railway KiHa 5010 series diesel railcar (かんとうてつどうキハ5010がたきどうしゃ) is a commuter-type diesel railcar of Kantō Railway.

== Overview ==
It was built to replace the KiHa 100 series, which were former JNR KiHa 30 type diesel railcars converted for one-man operation, and it began commercial operation on February 25, 2017. It was built by Niigata Transys.

=== Until introduction ===
Until then, Kantō Railway had adopted only the DMF13 series made by Niigata Power Systems (now IHI Power Systems) for its completely newly built lightweight diesel railcars from the KiHa 2100 series to the KiHa 5000 series, and for engine replacements from the DMH17 series in existing cars such as the KiHa 0 type; however, for the first batch of the KiHa 2100 series, more than 20 years had passed since their introduction in 1993, and the engines they carried had become increasingly obsolete. Also, it was decided to adopt LED for the interior ceiling lighting, but whereas LED lighting was being adopted in rapid succession in electric cars in the early 2010s, its adoption in diesel railcars—especially general-purpose commuter diesel railcars—was almost nonexistent as of 2016 except for JR Central's KiHa 25 type; therefore, it was decided to first install it experimentally in an actual car and carry out running tests.
When adopting a new engine to replace the Niigata Power Systems DMF13 series (DMF13HZ), in the KiHa 2100 series set of 2101 and 2102, 2101 was re-engined with the SA6D125-HE2 type, a form of the Komatsu DMF11HZ series that would later be installed in this type, and at the same time the interior ceiling lighting was changed from fluorescent to LED, and from April 2016 long-term running tests were carried out while in commercial operation.
Reflecting the running tests with the KiHa 2100 series, it was designed as the de facto mass-production type that put into practical use, for a Kantō Railway car, the Komatsu DMF11HZ series engine and LED lighting.

=== Features ===
It is a double-ended cab car based on the KiHa 5000 series, but it differs from the conventional cars in the following points.
The livery is a two-tone of a white called "Kantetsu White" and a blue evoking the Kinu River and Kokai River along the Jōsō Line, with a golden line evoking "rice ears waving over the rich earth" placed on the waist of the body, and a mark evoking the fresh green of Mount Tsukuba placed on the door pocket of the single sliding door on the driver's cab side.
The engine was changed to the Komatsu SA6D125-HE2 type, rated at 355 hp and equipped with a common-rail fuel control system (the first adoption of a Komatsu SA6D125 series engine by a private railway).
The LED-type next-station indicator is installed on only one of the doors. Above the door where it is not installed, only a list of stopping stations is installed.
The installation position of the numbered-ticket issuing machine was changed to only one place near the fare box.
LED conversion of the interior ceiling lighting.
The color of the seat upholstery was returned to the red used up to the KiHa 2400 series.
The window support method of the passenger doors was also returned to the same as the conventional cars up to the KiHa 2400 series.
The straps were changed to a two-tier shape.
A door-opening warning light was installed above the passenger doors on the interior side, and a yellow caution film was affixed to the door-pocket side of the passenger doors.
The fare display of the one-man equipment was changed to a liquid-crystal type.
For the bogies, as before, the powered bogie is the NF01HD type and the trailer bogie is the NF01HT type, but snow-resistant brakes have been added.
The one-man operation provisions are the same.

== Present ==
Currently, a total of two cars, KiHa 5011 and KiHa 5012, are in service, operating on the Jōsō Line. From February 26 to March 3, 2017, the scheduled operating times of this type were posted on the Kantō Railway website.
